items.description: One test on one column's raw cells. A null or NaN cell passes only ``is_null``.

op.description: The test. ``eq`` to ``ge`` compare each cell with ``value``; ``in`` and ``not_in`` check it against a list; ``is_null`` and ``not_null`` read no value. No string matching or regex.

value.description: What the cells are tested against. One value for ``eq`` to ``ge``, a list of up to 100 for ``in`` and ``not_in``, null for ``is_null`` and ``not_null``. A numeric column takes numbers, a text column strings, a bool column bools; other columns take only ``is_null`` and ``not_null``.

filter.description: An OR of up to 5 AND-lists, each of 1 to 10 ``{"column": ..., "op": ..., "value": ...}`` predicates. A row matches when every predicate of any one list passes. The ops are ``eq``, ``ne``, ``lt``, ``le``, ``gt``, ``ge``, ``in`` (up to 100 values), ``not_in``, ``is_null`` and ``not_null``. A null or NaN cell passes only ``is_null``. A declared sentinel is a value like any other, so ``is_null`` can disagree with the profile's null ratio. Null keeps every row. Constraints: at least 1 items; at most 5 items; at least 1 items; at most 10 items.

anyOf.description: Return rows: each chosen column's cells, one per returned row.

columns.description: The columns to return, in this order. Null means every column. At most 10 are returned, the first 10 named; ``omitted`` counts the rest.

limit.description: Most rows to return, from 1 to 50. Null means 20. Constraints: at least 1; at most 50.

anyOf.description: The first rows, in the order the frame holds them.
A seeded random sample of the matching rows, in drawn order.

seed.description: Seed of the draw, from 0 to 4294967295. The same seed on the same frame and filter draws the same rows. Null means a fixed default. Constraints: at least 0; at most 4294967295.

anyOf.description: The matching rows sorted by one column. Null and NaN cells come last; ties keep dataset order.

direction.description: ``ascending`` puts the smallest first, ``descending`` the largest. Null means ``ascending``.

order.description: Which matching rows to return: ``dataset`` takes the first, ``random`` a seeded sample, ``sort`` the top by one column. Null means ``dataset``.

anyOf.description: Return measures of the matching rows, one value per group.

group_by.description: Up to 3 key columns; each distinct combination of their values is a group, a null key included. Null or empty means the matching rows are one group. Constraints: at most 3 items.

items.description: One measure of one column, taken over each group's rows.

fn.description: ``count`` counts the cells that are not null, ``null_count`` those that are, ``nunique`` the distinct values that are not null. ``sum``, ``mean``, ``std`` (sample), ``min``, ``max`` and ``median`` read numeric columns only and skip null cells. NaN counts as null.

measures.description: Up to 5 measures, returned in this order within ``measures`` and ``literal_measures``. Null means none: only the group sizes. Constraints: at most 5 items.

mode.description: Rows mode is ``{"kind": "rows", "columns": [...], "limit": n, "order": {...}}``. ``columns`` null means every column, at most 10 returned; ``limit`` null means 20, at most 50. ``order`` is ``{"kind": "dataset"}`` (the default), ``{"kind": "random", "seed": n}`` (null seed means a fixed default, so the same call draws the same rows) or ``{"kind": "sort", "column": ..., "direction": "descending"}`` (null direction means ascending; null and NaN cells last, ties in dataset order). Aggregate mode is ``{"kind": "aggregate", "group_by": [...], "measures": [{"column": ..., "fn": ...}]}`` with up to 3 ``group_by`` columns (empty means one group of every matching row) and up to 5 measures: ``count``, ``null_count``, ``nunique``, and on numeric columns ``sum``, ``mean``, ``std``, ``min``, ``max`` and ``median``. NaN counts as null. Null means rows mode with every default.

output.description: Raw cells or grouped measures from a frame, laid out by column. Read row or group ``i`` as ``values[i]`` of every column.

warnings.description: Caveats on this result, most actionable first. Empty when there are none.

fields.description: Always exactly `code`, `message`, `columns`, `param`, `hint`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: A caveat on a successful result: it worked, but read this first. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `code`: The warning's Error Code. Branch on this, not on ``message``.
Position 1, `message`: What happened and what to do, in one or two sentences.
Position 2, `columns`: Columns the warning concerns, or null.
Position 3, `param`: The argument the warning concerns, or null.
Position 4, `hint`: Library-written advice, or null.

omitted.description: One entry per list that was cut, naming the Operation that returns the rest. Empty when nothing was cut.

fields.description: Always exactly `field`, `shown`, `total`, `operation`, `reason`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: Something left out of a result: a capped list was cut, or a Literal Field withheld. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `field`: Name of the list field that was cut, or the path of the Literal Field withheld, such as ``top_values[].value``.
Position 1, `shown`: How many items the list holds; 0 for a withheld Literal Field or cut cells.
Position 2, `total`: How many items exist; for a withheld Literal Field, how many values at that path are null; for cut cells, how many were cut.
Position 3, `operation`: The Operation that returns the rest, or null when no Operation does.
Position 4, `reason`: ``cap`` when a list was cut to its cap; ``literal_policy`` when the Operator's Literal Policy is ``deny``; ``truncated`` when long text cells were cut to their character cap.

matched_rows.description: Rows that match the filter, counted exactly over every row, past any cap. With no filter, every row matches.

row_positions.description: Rows mode: each returned row's position in the frame, from 0, in returned order. When more rows match, ``omitted`` counts them. Null in aggregate mode.

group_count.description: Aggregate mode: how many groups the matching rows form, counted exactly, past the cap of 100. Null in rows mode.

group_sizes.description: Aggregate mode: each returned group's row count, largest first, ties in key order with null keys last. At most 100; ``omitted`` counts the rest. Null in rows mode.

columns.description: Rows mode: the chosen columns, in the order asked, or in dataset order, at most 10; ``omitted`` counts the rest. Aggregate mode: the ``group_by`` keys, one value per group.

fields.description: Always exactly `kind`, `name`, `dtype`, `values`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: One column's raw cells: one per returned row, or one group key per group. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `kind`: Always ``cells``: raw cells of a column.
Position 1, `name`: Column name.
Position 2, `dtype`: The column's storage type, such as ``Int64``, ``Float64`` or ``String``.

Position 3, `values`: The cells as stored, one per entry of ``row_positions`` or ``group_sizes``, in that order. Missing cells and NaN are null; datetimes are ISO text; text over 64 characters is cut and counted in ``omitted``. A Literal Field.

measures.description: Aggregate mode: the counts and statistics asked for, in the order asked. Empty in rows mode.

fields.description: Always exactly `kind`, `column`, `fn`, `values`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: One measure that is a count or a statistic no cell need equal, one value per group. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `kind`: Always ``measure``: ``count``, ``null_count``, ``nunique``, ``sum``, ``mean`` or ``std``.
Position 1, `column`: The column measured.
Position 2, `fn`: The measure.
Position 3, `values`: One value per entry of ``group_sizes``, in that order. Null when the group has no value to measure, such as ``std`` of one cell.

literal_measures.description: Aggregate mode: the ``min``, ``max`` and ``median`` measures asked for, in the order asked. Empty in rows mode.

fields.description: Always exactly `kind`, `column`, `fn`, `values`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: One measure whose value can equal a cell, one value per group. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `kind`: Always ``literal_measure``: ``min``, ``max`` or ``median``.
Position 1, `column`: The column measured.
Position 2, `fn`: The measure.
Position 3, `values`: One value per entry of ``group_sizes``, in that order. Null when the group has no cell to measure. A Literal Field.
